module_title: Tribes and Folk Traditions of UP - Foundational Matrix (Core Demographics & Cultural Anchors)
introduction: Although Scheduled Tribes (ST) constitute a mere 0.57% of Uttar Pradesh's total population, their cultural footprint in the Terai and Vindhya regions is profound. At this foundational level, we will memorize the largest tribes and the most famous regional folk songs and dances that frequently appear in 'Match the Following' questions.

core_concepts.title: Major Tribes of Uttar Pradesh
core_concepts.description:
- **Tharu Tribe:** The **largest tribe** in UP. They primarily inhabit the Terai region (Maharajganj, Siddharthnagar, Shravasti, Lakhimpur Kheri). A highly tested fact is that Tharus observe **Diwali as a festival of mourning (Shoka)** and celebrate the 'Bajhar' festival.
- **Buksa (Bhoksa) Tribe:** Concentrated mainly in the **Bijnor** district. Their social structure resembles that of Rajputs (Patwar), and they practice Anuloma-Pratiloma (hypergamy/hypogamy) marriages.
- **Kharwar Tribe:** Found in the **Sonbhadra** and Ballia regions. Known for their fierce bravery and quick temper. Their most famous cultural expression is the **Karma dance**.

core_concepts.title: Prominent Regional Folk Songs
core_concepts.description:
- **Alha:** Bundelkhand (Mahoba region). A heroic ballad (Veer Ras) narrating the martial exploits of the legendary warrior brothers, Alha and Udal.
- **Kajri:** Mirzapur and Varanasi. A romantic folk song sung by women during the monsoon (Sawan) season.
- **Birha:** Purvanchal (Bhojpuri region). The signature folk song of the Ahir (Yadav) community, deeply rooted in the emotion of separation (Viraha).
- **Rasiya:** Braj Region (Mathura, Barsana). Devotional-romantic songs celebrating the divine love of Lord Krishna and Radha.

core_concepts.title: Signature Regional Folk Dances
core_concepts.description:
- **Charkula:** Braj Region. A spectacular dance where veiled women balance a heavy multi-tiered wooden pyramid (chariot wheel) holding 108 lit oil lamps on their heads.
- **Rai Dance:** Bundelkhand. Performed by women of the region mimicking a peacock during the festival of Krishna Janmashtami.
- **Katghorwa:** Purvanchal. An entertaining ceremonial dance where the dancer wears a wooden horse carcass (dummy horse) around their waist.

important_entities.name: Sonbhadra
important_entities.significance: Sonbhadra is statistically the most important district for this topic, boasting both the **highest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population** and the **highest ST percentage** in Uttar Pradesh. (Conversely, Baghpat has the lowest).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Why do Tharus mourn on Diwali? The exam often asks for the reason. They do not hate the festival; rather, they use this specific day to offer tributes and food to their deceased ancestors, observing it as a day of remembrance (Shoka) rather than celebration.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use these simple two-letter acronyms to instantly lock in the correct geographical region for UP's biggest folk songs during matching questions.

exam_strategy_tips: In RO/ARO and UP Police exams, pairing 'Kajri' with Mirzapur and 'Charkula' with the Braj region are the most recycled questions. Additionally, the district of the Buksa tribe (Bijnor) is highly tested.
